items.title: Agents
items.summary: Intelligent agents are considered by many to be the ultimate goal of AI. The classic book by Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (Prentice Hall, 1995), defines the field of AI research as “ the study and design of rational agents. ” The unprecedented capabilities of foundation models have opened the door to agentic applications that were previously unimaginable. These new capabilities make it finally possible to develop autonomous, intelligent agents to act as our assistants, coworkers, and coaches.

items.title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN
items.summary: This paper presents AutoSec-RAN, a specification-grounded large language model (LLM) framework for automated security triage of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) testing. Unlike approaches relying on static rule sets or privileged access to raw packet captures, AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct through two Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) stages over a curated corpus of 69 O-RAN, 3GPP, and adjacent standards documents, then selectively augments inference with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the same specification index.

items.title: Conflict-Aware Autonomous Resource Orchestration for 5G Edge Slicing Using Multi-Agent Systems and LLMs
items.summary: 5G edge network slicing must reconcile two coupled requirements: understanding high-level operator intent and reallocating scarce computing and bandwidth resources under dynamic contention. Centralized optimization can face computational and responsiveness challenges under rapidly changing edge contention, and Multi-Agent System (MAS)-based auctions can support resource arbitration but still depend on operator-defined economic parameters and priorities.

items.title: Line-Rate GTP-U Admission Control at the Edge of a Cloud-Native 5G Core: An XDP-Based Design for Kubernetes-Hosted User Plane Functions
items.summary: The User Plane Function (UPF) of a 5G Standalone core terminates every GPRS Tunnelling Protocol user-plane (GTP-U) packet arriving from the radio access network, which makes its N3 interface both the busiest and the most exposed point of the mobile data path. As operators migrate the core onto Kubernetes and public cloud, the UPF increasingly shares a general-purpose Linux kernel with other workloads, and kernel-bypass frameworks such as DPDK become harder to operate.

items.title: TRACE: Tackling Real-World Resource Assignment Problems via Agentic Heuristic Design
items.summary: Dynamic resource assignment, the real-time allocation of task streams to heterogeneous processing nodes, is the backbone of modern computing infrastructure. While learning-based schedulers excel in research, industrial deployments still rely on hand-written rules that operators can read, audit, and execute within tight latency budgets. LLM-based Automatic Heuristic Design (AHD) promises to automate writing such rules. However, existing AHD frameworks were developed for combinatorial problems fully specified to the LLM, and they learn only from a scalar fitness score.

items.title: AIR-LLM: Broadcasting AI Weights over Radio for Memory-Free Edge LLM Inference via RF Computing
items.summary: Next-generation large language models (LLMs) are expanding from the cloud to ubiquitous edge devices. However, edge devices typically either lack the memory to store increasingly large LLM weights or, even with enough memory, spend unaffordable energy on loading the weights. This raises our question: can an edge device run an LLM without storing or loading its weights, but receive them over the air and consume them on the fly? Inspired by wireless broadcasting, we present AIR-LLM, an LLM inference architecture for edge devices, which is composed of: (i) a central radio (e.g., 5G base…

items.title: Validating Memory-Optimal Transformer Kernels on Real Hardware: From Formal Derivation to Measured Performance Across Two HPC Clusters
items.summary: We validate memory-optimal cost functions for transformer kernels derived via the Mathematics of Arrays (MoA). Companion Papers I-IV formally derive kernels for attention forward, backward, fused forward+backward, decode, and the complete block (RMSNorm, gated MLP) as a hardware-independent specification (DNF) transformed to a machine-specific realization (ONF) via gamma, with verification to machine precision against PyTorch. This paper checks those predictions against measured performance on two HPC clusters (Purdue Anvil, NCSA Delta) across CPU and GPU. Three results stand out.

items.title: Computation-Limited Signals in Practice: A Throughput Anomaly in Software-Defined O-RAN PHY Layers
items.summary: We formalize a performance anomaly in software-based wireless physical-layer (PHY) implementations, a key enabling technology for Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) systems. For a fixed offered load, the number of PHY symbols required to transmit the load decreases as the nominal bit rate increases because each symbol conveys more bits. Shorter bursts, however, provide fewer opportunities to exploit pipelined modulation, transmission, and demodulation.

items.title: TriSLA: A Preventive and Closed-Loop SLA-Aware Architecture for Multidomain Decision-Making with Explainable Artificial Intelligence in 5G Networks
items.summary: Network slicing in multidomain 5G environments introduces critical challenges in guaranteeing Service Level Agreements (SLAs) under dynamic resource variability and heterogeneous service requirements. This article presents TriSLA, a closed-loop, preventive, SLA-aware architecture designed to evaluate feasibility at request time and continuously ensure SLA compliance during operation.

items.title: Free-Text Evaluation of LLMs for 5G Domain Knowledge and Fault Analysis using LLM-as-Judge
items.summary: Real-world fault analysis in 5G and emerging 6G networks demands domain expertise to analyze free-text diagnostics, including root-cause explanations and recommended actions. LLMs have emerged as a promising approach to automating this, yet whether lightweight, edge-deployable models are capable of performing in-depth free-text diagnostics remains an open question. While existing benchmarks rely on restrictive MCQs with fixed answer keys, this paper evaluates 5G domain understanding and fault analysis in a free-text generation format.

items.title: Explainability Boosted Anomaly Detection Framework for O-RAN based NextG Networks
items.summary: The wireless networks have historically faced significant security vulnerabilities, necessitating advanced anomaly detection mechanisms, especially as networks evolve towards 6G and beyond. This study introduces an advanced anomaly detection framework that leverages explainable artificial intelligence to enhance the security of next-generation (NextG) cellular networks.

items.title: FedRIC: Heterogeneity-Aware Federated Learning with Hard Deadline Constraints in Open RAN
items.summary: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) bring intelligence to disaggregated RANs through virtualized platforms and open interfaces, but the stringent latency budgets of the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) and heterogeneous traffic conditions make real-time deployment costly. Centralized learning is ill-suited to the RIC due to its computational burden, timing constraints, and communication overhead, motivating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed alternative.

items.title: AutoSec-RAN: Specification-Grounded LLM Fine-Tuning for Automated Security Analysis of O-RAN
items.summary: This paper presents AutoSec-RAN, a specification-grounded large language model (LLM) framework for automated security triage of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) testing. Unlike approaches relying on static rule sets or privileged access to raw packet captures, AutoSec-RAN fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct through two Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) stages over a curated corpus of 69 O-RAN, 3GPP, and adjacent standards documents, then selectively augments inference with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the same specification index.

items.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Testing and Automation of Open RAN Systems: GNG-OTA Framework
items.summary: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) empower operators with choice and customization through their disaggregated and interoperable architecture. However, ensuring interoperability in O-RAN presents challenges due to complex testing environments and evolving specifications. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing the Generative AI and Graph Neural Network-based Open RAN Testing and Automation (GNG-OTA) framework.

items.title: Cost-Aware Conflict Triage for xApp Control Conflicts in Open RAN
items.summary: Open Radio Access Network (Open RAN) enables multi-vendor deployments where concurrent RAN control applications (xApps) independently optimise mobility, load, coverage, and energy within the Near Real Time RAN Intelligent Controller (Near-RT RIC). When xApps act on overlapping control parameters, their isolated loops produce conflicting decisions that degrade the network Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Existing conflict-evaluation methods estimate severity but do not answer whether the intervention is cost-justified.

items.title: A QoE-Driven Framework for O-RAN Network Slicing Based on Empirical Multi-User VR Traffic Modelling
items.summary: Virtual Reality (VR) requires strict Quality-of-Experience (QoE) guarantees, making radio resource management harder. Static slice allocations are wasteful, while dynamic approaches often rely on heuristic penalty functions lacking an empirical basis. We introduce a QoE-driven network-slicing framework for Open RAN in which resource allocation is guided by empirically derived multi-user VR traffic statistics. Closed-form n-fold convolutions model the aggregate data rate and inter-arrival time of n concurrent users, validated empirically for up to four.

items.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
items.summary: Here's a product feature which the world is going to need a whole lot more of over the coming months and years: default hard budget caps . I'm talking about the feature of pay-by-usage services and APIs that lets you say "after $X/month, cut this thing off and return errors". These need to be hard limits. Soft caps, "after $X/month, send me a warning email", will not cut it. Coding agents, and personal agents (coding agents wrapped in a less threatening UI), greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code that can do useful things.

items.summary: Matthew Green has been writing a rather pessimistic series of posts about the potential for AI systems to vastly outperform humans in cryptanalysis of both symmetric and public-key ciphers. I am more optimistic than he is. That is, I have stronger faith in the over-engineering cryptographers tend to do. I am trying to write this up in more detail.

items.title: Cyberattack on Connected Fridges in France
items.summary: Another IoT cyberattack , this one in France: Hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight, according to one supermarket chain affected. […] Normally, supermarket freezers go through a short period of defrosting overnight, in which temperatures rise slightly. But the hackers ordered the units to heat up and stay hot, although Danfoss did not confirm any reports about just how warm the fridges and freezers could become in that process.

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: I Caught a Squid
items.summary: On Wednesday I spent a day fishing, on a small boat out of Gloucester, MA. We caught many cod (none of which we could keep), and a bunch of hake and mackerel (all of which we could keep). And…I caught a squid! Near as I can tell, it’s a longfin squid, sometimes called a Boston squid ( Doryteuthis (Amerigo) pealeii ). That night I cooked it over a barbecue grill—hot and fast. Delicious.

items.title: When AI Agents Obey the Wrong Master
items.summary: The Double-Edged Sword of Instruction-Following and How to Detect Attacks That Hide Across Time Large Language Models have proven themselves truly remarkable — from writing text and generating images, to analyzing and summarizing information and performing increasingly sophisticated reasoning and decision-making as they race toward fully autonomous AI Agents. But all of these impressive abilities share one foundational characteristic: LLMs are trained, above all else, to follow instructions.

items.title: Scaling E2E Tests for Multi-Tenant SaaS with Playwright
items.summary: Master tenant isolation and dynamic project generation to orchestrate reliable parallel tests across every region and configuration. Note: This post is the second in a two-part series. In Part 1 , we built the authentication and feature-toggle retrieval flow for a micro-frontend system. Most end-to-end pipelines assume a single authentication flow and one set of feature flags. That works when testing one user or one tenant, but it fails in a multi-tenant SaaS platform where each tenant has its own configuration, credentials, feature toggles and perhaps hosted on a different region.

items.title: Byte Language Models: Scaling, Emergent Abstractions, and Information Allocation
items.summary: The paper challenges the assumption that language models need explicit tokenizers to be efficient demonstrating that standard flat Transformers can process raw byte sequences and actually outperform traditional subword models as parameter sizes scale. The prevailing thought in the field has been that processing raw bytes is computationally inefficient because the sequences are substantially longer. A typical subword contains around four bytes. The authors argue that this extra sequence length is actually a feature that provides useful additional computation under the same parameter budget.
